summary: Backend-only verification of the logger-scope NameError fix in /app/backend/server.py. All 7 pytest cases pass against the external URL (root, GET /api/status, POST /api/status persistence, /api/pinky/auth text/voice/default/invalid-mode). Error path was explicitly simulated by temporarily swapping ELEVENLABS_API_KEY with an invalid value and calling both text and voice modes: both returned HTTP 401 with valid JSON detail 'Invalid API key' and emitted proper ERROR log lines via logger — NO NameError. Original API key restored, /api/pinky/auth?mode=text back to 200. Deployment blocker resolved.
verified_behaviors: POST /api/status {client_name:'TEST_deploy-test'} -> 200 with id, timestamp, echoed client_name; item present on subsequent GET /api/status
GET /api/pinky/auth?mode=text -> 200, signed_url starts with wss://, conversation_token is null, agent_id starts with 'agent_'
GET /api/pinky/auth?mode=voice -> 200, conversation_token is non-empty JWT-like string, signed_url is null
GET /api/pinky/auth (no mode) -> 200 and defaults to text

Error path (simulated invalid ELEVENLABS_API_KEY): text mode -> 401 JSON {detail:'Invalid API key'}, voice mode -> 401 JSON {detail:'Invalid API key'}, backend.err.log shows 'server - ERROR - ElevenLabs signed-url error: 401 ...' and 'server - ERROR - ElevenLabs token error: 401 ...' — logger is correctly in scope, no NameError
Backend supervisor startup clean, no NameError in backend.err.log
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 97: /api/pinky/auth is defined as sync def but calls blocking requests.get. Fine for current traffic but should migrate to async def + httpx.AsyncClient to avoid tying up the FastAPI thread pool on ElevenLabs latency.
server.py line 156: @app.on_event('shutdown') is deprecated in FastAPI/Starlette — migrate to the lifespan context manager pattern.
server.py line 26/28: os.environ['MONGO_URL']/['DB_NAME'] will hard-crash the process on missing env — good fail-fast, keep as is.

server.py: logger is now defined at line 23 (before any handler that references it) — NameError blocker fixed cleanly. Consider adding a unit test that mocks requests.get to force the error branch, so future regressions of logger scope are caught at test-time (currently we only verified via live invalid-key simulation).
seed_data_creation: One TEST_deploy-test status_checks doc inserted via POST /api/status; harmless.
context_for_next_testing_agent: NameError fix verified. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_pinky_auth.py now also covers /api/status POST+GET persistence and root. To reverify the error branch without swapping keys, mock requests.get inside an in-process test.
rca of the issue: Original blocker: logger was referenced at server.py lines 113 & 131 (error branches of /api/pinky/auth) but only assigned at line 154 — module load order meant the name existed by import time, but any check tool statically flagged it and the top-level ordering was inconsistent. Fix moved logging.basicConfig + logger = getLogger(__name__) to lines 19-23 immediately after load_dotenv. Verified via invalid-key simulation that both logger.error(...) calls execute and produce proper ERROR log lines with a JSON HTTP response — no NameError.
